sections.title: Core Foundations & Conceptual Framework
sections.content:
• **Instrument of Governance**: Commissions served as the primary tool for the British to legitimize policy shifts through 'expert' inquiry.
• **Evolutionary Trend**: Shifted from purely revenue-focused (early 19th century) to administrative/constitutional reform (late 19th/early 20th century).
• **Reporting Mechanism**: Most commissions were advisory; the British government retained the right to accept, reject, or modify recommendations.
• **Key Metric**: The 'Divide and Rule' policy was often operationalized through the recommendations of these commissions.

items.title: Major Applications / Initiatives
items.content:
• **Famine Codes**: Resulted from the Strachey Commission, establishing a systematic relief framework.
• **University Act (1904)**: Direct outcome of the Raleigh Commission, tightening government control over universities.

items.title: Challenges & Way Forward
items.content:
• **Key Challenges**: Lack of Indian representation in early commissions; focus on colonial interests over welfare.
• **Solutions**: Post-independence, these were replaced by constitutional bodies like the UPSC and Finance Commission.

items.title: Mnemonic for Retention
items.content:
• **Memory Acronym**: 'F-E-A-R' (Famine, Education, Administrative, Reform).
• **Decoded Meaning**: F (Famine: Campbell, Strachey), E (Education: Hunter, Raleigh), A (Administrative: Aitchison, Fraser), R (Reform: Decentralization, Royal Commission on Public Services).

upscNotes.content: Examiner Trap: Confusing the Hunter Commission (1882 - Education) with the Hunter Committee (1919 - Jallianwala Bagh Massacre). Always check the year.
Mains Value Addition: Use the term 'Colonial Institutionalization' to describe how these commissions created the bureaucratic framework that persists in modern India.

keyTakeaways: Commissions were used to legitimize colonial policy through the facade of scientific inquiry.
Chronology is the most important aspect for Prelims; focus on the Viceroy under whom the commission was formed.
Most commissions aimed to balance administrative efficiency with the maintenance of British hegemony.
